alt: Black Ring Smart Lock mounted on a wooden door, showing a stacked fingerprint reader and backlit keypad with the knurled power-generating dial below them
story: Ring's first smart lock ($249) solves the dead-battery lockout problem with a built-in power dial — turn it a few times and the crank generator gives the electronics just enough power to accept your PIN; founder Jamie Siminoff pitched the lock as the end of 'little pieces of metal in our pockets', but the backup when digital fails is manual cranking.
why_funny: The inventor's argument against physical keys is that they're primitive, yet his solution when the smart lock's battery dies is turning a hand crank like you're starting a 1920s motorcar.
